title: it, not who sold it, but who was allowed to keep built with Fable 5
author: Resight
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
Bund mein bagule baithe hain, lehron ka kya kasoor (the herons sit on the embankment; what fault is it of the waves?" The proverb is usually used for misplaced blame. Here it works in reverse. The waves, the millions of users in dozens of countries who lost access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 overnight, did nothing. The embankment moved.

A private company built something powerful enough that a government decided it needed to control who else got to use it... not who built it, not who sold it, but who was allowed to keep using it after the sale. That's not how oil works. That's not how airplanes work. That's how weapons work.

Technology has quietly become the only category of asset that can be repossessed after delivery.
